admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.decided: 2026-10-06, before any score row existed (the first scores land 2026-10-09)
admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.trial: one per (proposer, UTC day of the target); the day's outcome is the covered flag of one scored row drawn by lot: rows sorted by id, index = sha256(domain + '|' + day) mod n
admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.looks: the exact binomial tail P[X <= k], X ~ Binomial(m, claim), read only at m = 30·2^j trial days, against the bar 1/20 · 2^-(j+1); the bars sum to 1/20
admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.sticky: the first look at or under its bar prunes the proposer version for good; admission returns only as a new version with its own record
admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.stated: trial days are treated as independent (weather persists across days): a convention, not a theorem
admission-v1 (apps/janela/audit/placar.j.replaces: the row-level count (every scored row a trial, the tail read every day against 1/20) — replaced before it read any score, because one overflight scores many rows at once

observation-v1 (apps/janela/audit/observ.when: a target day is observed three days after it ends (the NOAA file's D+2 version or later: NOAA rewrites every file daily at ~11:12 UTC and the D+1 version is incomplete), days strictly in order, a 404 held for retry until the day is six days old
observation-v1 (apps/janela/audit/observ.kept: each pass's own points (t, lat, lon, swh mm, wind cm/s, km): the value re-checks from them; the mission files' sha256 pin the bytes as read, which NOAA's daily rewrite makes unreproducible

commit-margin-v1 (apps/janela/audit/comm.rule: a row is committed only when its target is at least one hour after madeAt; the Action pushes right after committing, so the push time proves every row predates its target

noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.target: Hs (m) measured by satellite altimeter: exact mean of NOAA RADS NRT 1 Hz values within 100 km of the site, over the pass whose mid-time is nearest the target time and within 3 h (>= 5 points)
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.proposer: NOAA GEFS-Wave (WAVEWATCH III, the 00 UTC run, 31 members: the control c00 and p01..p30, global 0.25°; AWS noaa-gefs-pds, public domain): order statistics 4 and 28 of the 31 sorted members at the site's model node — the central 25 of 31
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.why the claim: if the truth and the 31 members are exchangeable (the ensemble's own premise), the closed band between the k-th and the (m+1-k)-th of m sorted members covers with probability at least (m+1-2k)/(m+1): k = 4, m = 31 gives 24/32 = 3/4 exactly. The ECMWF proposer's 4/5 is its member fraction (40 of 50), above its own exchangeable value 39/51; it stays as committed. Each proposer is tested against its own claim; neither claim is a theorem about the sea.
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.node: the box node nearest the site that GEFS-Wave's control calls sea at +0 h (feed.py sea_index, the rule the ECMWF feed uses), on GEFS-Wave's own 0.25° grid; it may differ from the ECMWF node, and the target is the site's, so both providers meet the same satellite passes
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.steps: 0, 6, ..., 168 h of the 00 UTC run — the ECMWF feed's steps, so both providers are graded on the same target times
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.exact: every value is a GRIB2 packed integer, value = (R + X·2^E)/10^D (Hs: R = 0, E = 0, D = 2 — centimetres), X recovered from eccodes' decode and refused when no integer reproduces the value; checked 2026-10-07 against an independent decode of one field's JPEG 2000 code stream (OpenJPEG) and its bitmap: 565,283 of 565,283 sea points equal
noaa-gefs-c25of31 (apps/janela/audit/com.feed: corpus/janela/feed-noaa/YYYYMMDD.json.gz (apps/janela/audit/noaa.py), written once, every member kept; each row names its sha256 prefix. The deterministic GFS-Wave Hs at the same node rides each row as det; it is not the band

providers-v1 (apps/janela/app).decided: 2026-10-07, before any NOAA band is shown in the app
providers-v1 (apps/janela/app).raw: a provider's raw ensemble band (ECMWF's central 40 of 50, NOAA's central 25 of 31) is shown beside the forecast and graded on the PLACAR; it is never decided on. The app decides only with calibrated bands (a provider's forecast times the exact conformal interval of its own satellite matchups).
providers-v1 (apps/janela/app).two: where a place carries calibrated bands from two providers, the app decides on their union [min lo, max hi]: it covers whenever either covers, so its coverage is at least the larger of the two claims — never the narrower or the better-looking band. The union holds until a ranking rule is dated here, before any ranking is read.
providers-v1 (apps/janela/app).pruned: a calibrated band the PLACAR prunes leaves the union (bandset.withoutPruned), and the place decides on what remains

calibrated-noaa-v1 (apps/janela/audit/co.claim: (u - l)/(n + 1) >= 9/10 per cell, as stated in each row
calibrated-noaa-v1 (apps/janela/audit/co.sites: the eight open-sea sites of 2026-10-06; Sergipe-Alagoas is not calibrated for NOAA (its region stays ECMWF's)
calibrated-noaa-v1 (apps/janela/audit/co.measured: the ratio band is wider than ECMWF's at every site and lead (mean width over the bins 0, 24, 72, 120 and 156 h: 0.558 against 0.457): GFS-Wave's deterministic Hs tracks the altimeter less tightly than ECMWF's, and reads low at the equatorial margin (Potiguar at 24 h: 0.94-1.28)
calibrated-noaa-v1 (apps/janela/audit/co.decides: with calibrated-v1 under providers-v1: the union; measured on the 2026-10-07 day before it decided, the union moves 2,038 of 67,744 published letters, every one to INDEFINIDA (1,562 from LIBERADA, 453 from VETADA, 23 from SEM DADOS) — none flips

decision-level-v1 (apps/janela/audit/dec.decided: 2026-10-07, before any decision was graded (the first observed day is 2026-10-06, observed 2026-10-09; the first kept day is 2026-10-07)
decision-level-v1 (apps/janela/audit/dec.kept: the published decisions at the open-sea sites a satellite can see (field, platform, coast), every preset and criterion, from the app's day, written once to certs/janela-decisions/YYYYMMDD.json right after the day is built (janela-field is overwritten daily)
decision-level-v1 (apps/janela/audit/dec.graded: the Hs limit of each preset only (the variable the altimeter measures); a window step is observed when a pass's mid-time is within 3 h of it (the pass nearest, score.js's rule); the sea between steps is never decided, so never graded; a window is graded only if it starts at least an hour after the decisions were kept
decision-level-v1 (apps/janela/audit/dec.outcomes: LIBERADA: held (every observed step within the limit) or broke (some observed step outside); VETADA: confirmed (some observed step outside) or open (every step observed, all within); unseen otherwise; a day not yet observed waits
decision-level-v1 (apps/janela/audit/dec.stated: descriptive counts, never an admission: a day's windows overlap and share passes; a LIBERADA's wind limit is not graded here

providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.decided: 2026-10-07 — the operator: 'you decide the best and reliable; ask what Petrobras needs'
providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.criterion: what Petrobras needs, in order: a LIBERADA must hold (a window the sea breaks costs a shuttle tanker, a lift vessel or a PSV); then as many decisive windows as possible (waiting costs day rates and tank capacity); then a claim a marine warranty surveyor can re-check
providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.measured: certs/janela-providers-eval.json: both providers' 45,987 joined pairs, bands calibrated on the passes before 2025-07-01 and judged on the 21,259 after (15 months never seen); options ECMWF alone, NOAA alone, their mean (weight fixed on an inner split of the calibration years), and the union, each at miss 1/10, 1/20, 1/40
providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.result: the union at 1/10 (coverage 0.965, mean width 1.172 m) against ECMWF alone at 1/20 (0.962, 1.212 m) — the same reliability bracket: at Hs <= 2.0 m the same LIBERADA count (6,368 vs 6,370) with fewer than half of them broken (21 vs 46); at 2.5 m more LIBERADA (11,703 vs 11,610) and fewer broken (26 vs 40); at 1.5 m 4.6% fewer LIBERADA, half broken (12 vs 23), none by more than 10% (vs 7). The providers' mean at 1/20 gives 3% more LIBERADA at 2.0 m with 1.8x the broken rate (38/6,554). Against ECMWF alone at 1/10, the union cuts broken LIBERADA at 2.0 m from 1.10% to 0.33% for 19% fewer LIBERADA
providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.decision: providers-v1 stands: the union of the two calibrated bands decides — the most reliable LIBERADA of the options at any decisiveness measured; and the union is graded as itself (union-v1), so the band that decides is the band on the scoreboard
providers-eval-v1 (apps/janela/audit/pro.stated: point-level (one step); a window needs every step, so window rates are higher in the same order; a statistical evaluation in floating point, not a certificate

union-v1 (apps/janela/audit/commit.js).target: Hs (m) measured by satellite altimeter: exact mean of NOAA RADS NRT 1 Hz values within 100 km of the site, over the pass whose mid-time is nearest the target time and within 3 h (>= 5 points)
